AF36 is one of the cleanest falsification cases for 'silent BGC' language. It is not simply silent: a G→A SNP at nucleotide 591 of aflC/pksA creates a premature stop codon, preventing functional PKS production and aflatoxin accumulation. The strain remains ecologically competitive and is exploited commercially precisely because of this stable non-aflatoxigenic phenotype.

Lovastatin biosynthesis is a particularly strong example of why gene-cluster presence alone is insufficient. LovB executes an iterative nonaketide programme but depends on the trans-acting enoyl reductase LovC because its own ER-like domain is inactive; LovG releases dihydromonacolin L and improves LovB turnover. LovA then performs two sequential oxidative transformations to monacolin J. Independently, LovF synthesizes a 2-methylbutyryl side chain, retained on its ACP, and LovD transfers it to monacolin J to yield lovastatin. The MIBiG sequence omits LovB, so pathway-level curation must cross accession boundaries.

MPA biosynthesis begins with MpaC making 5-methylorsellinic acid. The natural fusion MpaDE hydroxylates this intermediate and promotes lactonization to DHMP. Golgi-associated MpaA farnesylates DHMP; ER-bound MpaB then performs oxidative cleavage of the farnesyl side chain. MpaG can methylate several intermediates, creating pathway-order flexibility. The shortened methylated intermediate is handed to peroxisomal primary β-oxidation machinery, which generates MPA-CoA, and peroxisomal MpaH hydrolyzes it to MPA. MpaF is a resistant IMPDH paralog that protects the producer rather than building the molecule.

PtaA initiates an emodin-family nonreducing-PKS route, with PtaB/C/D/F forming the conserved early aromatic scaffold chemistry. One or both of PtaH/PtaI methylate the aromatic intermediates, and PtaJ contributes oxidative ring cleavage to a benzophenone/isosulochrin-type state. PtaM chlorinates isosulochrin-like substrate to chloroisosulochrin, while PtaE catalyzes oxidative phenol coupling to the diphenyl-ether product; the order of halogenation and coupling is flexible enough that nonchlorinated RES-1214-1 can also be oxidized before PtaM yields pestheic acid. This is a strong example of branching reaction order rather than one obligatory linear path.

Sol1 builds desmethylprosolanapyrone I from one acetyl-CoA and seven malonyl-CoA units with internal methylation. Sol2 O-methylates this to prosolanapyrone I; Sol6 hydroxylates to prosolanapyrone II. Sol5 oxidizes the alcohol to the reactive prosolanapyrone III state and catalyzes stereoselective [4+2] cycloaddition to solanapyrones A/D. Sol3 reduces the aldehyde congeners to B/E. Native Δsol5 mutants lose solanapyrones but remain pathogenic, while A. oryzae reconstitution reveals that expression host chemistry can oxidize intermediates or nonenzymatically convert solanapyrone A to solanapyrone C. AdaA builds the decaketide on its ACP. AdaC introduces the critical C2 hydroxylation while the chain is still ACP-bound. That α-hydroxylation changes the chemistry available to AdaB: without it, AdaB hydrolytically releases a tricyclic anthracenone-like product; with it, AdaB strongly promotes C18–C1 Claisen-like fourth-ring closure to the naphthacenedione scaffold. AdaD then performs C9 O-methylation to complete TAN-1612, while AdaR activates the locus. This is a rare case where a single oxidation event acts as a mechanistic switch controlling whether the same trans-acting release enzyme hydrolyzes or cyclizes the PKS product.

The terrein system is one of the strongest empirical examples for the Access Atlas concept. Glucose minimal medium leaves the pathway near-off, whereas plant juices, methionine, nitrogen limitation and iron starvation activate terR through distinct global regulatory routes. TerR directly activates the local cluster. TerA and TerB then collaborate physically/chemically to make 6-hydroxymellein; TerC performs oxidative decarboxylation and TerD a subsequent hydroxylation, while later oxidase steps remain incompletely assigned. The final metabolite acts extracellularly: it damages plant tissue, inhibits competitors and reduces Fe3+ to Fe2+, with a growth benefit under iron limitation when the siderophore pathway is defective. This record therefore spans signal access, transcription, enzyme cooperation, metabolic execution, export/recovery and ecological function in one system.

Ywa1 is a naphthopyrone pigment made by a fungal PKS. In the defining Paecilomyces variotii study, CRISPR deletion identified the pigment PKS and heterologous expression in Aspergillus nidulans identified its product as Ywa1. Those direct data are retained as literature provenance and are not transferred as strain-specific proof for the retired Byssochlamys accession.

The canonical retired source interval contains a PKS candidate associated with Ywa1. Direct gene-function evidence in the cited study pertains to the Paecilomyces variotii pigment PKS; exact orthology and one-to-one strain-specific causality for Byssochlamys sp. IMV 00236 remain UNCERTAIN.
The cited Paecilomyces study examined pigmentation and UV resistance rather than a cryptic-pathway activation programme. Native activation conditions for the retired Byssochlamys record are NR.

For Paecilomyces variotii: CRISPR-Cas9 gene deletion, UV-irradiation phenotype testing and heterologous PKS expression. For the exact retired Byssochlamys record: direct experimental linkage is UNCERTAIN from the canonical evidence package.
NR for native Ywa1 titer in Byssochlamys sp. IMV 00236.
Ywa1 pigmentation contributes to UV protection in Paecilomyces variotii. No strain-specific ecological-role claim is transferred to Byssochlamys sp. IMV 00236.

An NRPS-centered pathway builds the oxepinamide precursor, after which cytochrome P450 enzymes catalyze the key oxidative ring-expansion chemistry that generates the oxepin moiety with strong stereo- and regioselectivity.

The MIBiG locus contains the core NRPS and associated tailoring genes. P450 enzymes are directly demonstrated to mediate oxepin-ring formation; untested auxiliary-gene functions are retained as UNCERTAIN.
Native genetics plus heterologous expression and biochemical assays were used for pathway access; no separate environmental activation trigger is established.
gene deletion; heterologous expression; precursor-feeding experiments; enzyme assays; metabolite structure elucidation.
NR for standardized oxepinamide D production titer in current MIBiG.
Native ecological role of oxepinamide D remains UNCERTAIN in the pathway study.

Comparison of biruloquinone-producing and nonproducing lichen-forming fungal cultures identified PKS21/brq5 as the uniquely strong PKS expression correlate and a six-gene brq1-brq6 coexpressed locus. A polyketide route was proposed, but enzyme order remains inferential.

brq5/PKS21: candidate nonreducing PKS; brq1-brq4 and brq6: coexpressed neighboring genes with predicted tailoring roles. Specific catalytic assignments are prediction-level unless independently demonstrated.
Biruloquinone-producing versus nonproducing axenic chemotypes provided the physiological contrast; no engineered activation or direct regulator manipulation was required.
axenic chemotype comparison; RNA-seq; PKS phylogeny; locus coexpression analysis; comparative synteny.
The defining transcriptomic study reports strong differential expression across the brq locus; exact standardized biruloquinone production titer is NR in current MIBiG.
Biruloquinone is a rare lichen phenanthraquinone pigment; its native ecological function remains UNCERTAIN.

mRNA-seq in a signaling mutant that loses dibenzodioxocinone production defined a 21-gene pks8-centered cluster. Disruption of genes in that cluster caused loss of the metabolites, establishing pathway involvement; the detailed biosynthetic sequence proposed in the paper remained speculative.

pks8: core polyketide synthase genetically required for dibenzodioxocinone production; the larger 21-gene locus contains predicted tailoring/regulatory functions. Later work identifies DibT as a broad transcriptional regulator whose manipulation changes pks8-cluster expression, but those data derive from Pestalotiopsis microspora.

The defining discovery exploited a gα-signaling mutant with halted product formation; later DibT overexpression increased cluster expression and product yields in P. microspora. These regulatory findings are not silently transferred to the MIBiG-listed species.
mRNA-seq; signaling-mutant comparison; targeted cluster-gene disruption; metabolite profiling; later transcription-factor disruption/overexpression studies.

Earlier P. microspora work reported pestalotiollide B up to 7.22 mg/L in liquid culture, and deletion of competing pks35 increased it by 887%; these are contextual measurements from P. microspora NK17, not direct titers for the current Neopestalotiopsis record.
Dibenzodioxocinones are reported CETP-inhibitory natural products; native ecological function remains UNCERTAIN.

The four-gene tpcA-D cassette is sufficient for total biosynthesis of (-)-terpestacin in A. oryzae. TpcA constructs preterpestacin I; TpcB and TpcC perform stereo- and regioselective C-H hydroxylations; TpcD oxidizes the vicinal diol to an α-diketone followed by spontaneous/chemical enolization to terpestacin.
tpcA: bifunctional terpene synthase; tpcB/tpcC: cytochrome P450 monooxygenases installing three A-ring hydroxyls; tpcD: flavin-dependent oxidase converting vicinal diol to α-diketone.
Artificial pathway reconstruction by heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae establishes biosynthetic sufficiency; native Bipolaris activation/regulation is not resolved.
stepwise heterologous expression of tpcA-D; intermediate isolation; metabolite profiling; structural characterization.
NR for native Bipolaris terpestacin titer in current MIBiG.
Terpestacin is an antiangiogenic natural product; native ecological role in Bipolaris maydis remains UNCERTAIN.

BGC0002246 is the H. sublateritium FD-334 SS-4 genomic region homologous to the H. fasciculare Hfas344 naematolin candidate locus. The defining study experimentally characterized the H. fasciculare ortholog: its atypical sesquiterpene synthase generates caryophyllene-related scaffolds and co-expression with the adjacent FAD oxidase yields oxidized cariolan/caryophyllane derivatives. These experiments support the early biogenetic logic but do not constitute complete heterologous biosynthesis of naematolin from the H. sublateritium locus.

Hsub99-region sesquiterpene synthase: homologous candidate for the unusual caryophyllane-forming cyclase; adjacent candidate tailoring genes include an FAD oxidoreductase, aldo-keto reductase, zinc-dependent carboxypeptidase, zinc alcohol dehydrogenase and cytochrome P450 oxidoreductases. Direct catalytic assignments were demonstrated for the H. fasciculare orthologous synthase/FAD-oxidase pair, not individually for every H. sublateritium gene.

Naematolin was detected from cultured H. sublateritium and H. fasciculare in YMG liquid medium. Pathway access experiments used Aspergillus oryzae heterologous expression of H. fasciculare candidate genes; native transcriptional regulation or environmental gating of the H. sublateritium locus was not resolved.

LC-MS purification plus HRMS/IR/NMR confirmation of native naematolin; comparative genome mining between two producing Hypholoma species; heterologous expression of candidate sesquiterpene synthases in A. oryzae; co-expression of the H. fasciculare Hfas344 cyclase with adjacent FAD oxidase; GC-MS/LC-MS and structural characterization of oxidized products.

Native naematolin: LC-MS retention time approximately 12.25 min; purified compound HRMS m/z 331.1522 as sodium adduct, consistent with C17H24NaO5. Defining study describes native titres as low but does not provide a validated H. sublateritium production titer in the canonical record.

Naematolin is a biologically active caryophyllane sesquiterpene. Disc diffusion in the defining study showed limited antibacterial activity against Bacillus subtilis and Staphylococcus aureus and no activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa or Klebsiella pneumoniae; native ecological function in Hypholoma is UNCERTAIN.

BGC0002247 is a retired historical PKS/NRPS record associated with chaetoconvosins A/B, chamiside A and naematolin in Amesia nigricolor. Because the current canonical record is retired and no defining complete pathway reconstruction was located, the locus is retained as provenance metadata rather than an active causal BGC assignment.

Historical MIBiG class metadata indicates PKS and NRPS biosynthetic capacity, but gene-level catalytic assignments are not promoted here because current retirement removes the basis for treating the historical locus as a validated active pathway.

Amesia nigricolor cultures have yielded chamiside- and chaetoconvosin-family metabolites. Native regulatory triggers, transcriptional activation of the retired locus and causal locus-to-product perturbation are NR.

Natural-product isolation and structure elucidation support compound occurrence; canonical retirement was checked separately. No knockout, targeted activation or complete heterologous reconstruction is used as evidence for this retired accession.
NR for a validated locus-specific production titer in the retired canonical record.
Chaetoconvosin B has reported phytotoxic/root-growth inhibitory and cytotoxic activities; such compound-level bioactivity does not establish the ecological role of BGC0002247 in Amesia.

BGC0002248 encodes flavunoidine biosynthesis in Aspergillus flavus NRRL3357. The defining study used heterologous expression and metabolite characterization to assign the pathway enzymes and establish the biosynthetic sequence underlying the terpene/NRPS-derived natural product.

The flv locus combines terpene-forming machinery with NRPS-associated chemistry, including enzymes required for the unusual 5,5-dimethylpipecolate-containing architecture. Individual flv roles were resolved experimentally in the defining reconstruction rather than inferred solely from annotation.

Pathway chemistry was accessed through heterologous expression. This demonstrates biosynthetic competence and sufficiency of the encoded machinery but does not by itself define native environmental or transcriptional activation gates in A. flavus.
Genome mining, stepwise heterologous expression, metabolite profiling, isolation and structural characterization of pathway products/intermediates.
NR for a validated native A. flavus flavunoidine titer in the current canonical record.
Flavunoidine is a structurally unusual fungal natural product; a native ecological function for the pathway is not established by the defining biosynthetic experiments.

BGC0002249 represents the phaeospelide A pathway from Arthrinium phaeospermum. The defining work supports a compact two-enzyme logic in which the polyketide synthase ApmlA builds the precursor and the trans-acting thioesterase ApmlB promotes release/macrocyclization.
ApmlA: fungal polyketide synthase constructing the polyketide chain; ApmlB: trans-acting thioesterase involved in product release and macrocyclization to the macrolide scaffold.
Pathway function was interrogated by heterologous expression, providing direct access to biosynthetic chemistry; native regulatory activation in A. phaeospermum was not resolved.
Heterologous expression of pathway components, metabolite analysis, product isolation and structure elucidation.
NR for a validated native phaeospelide A production titer in the current canonical record.
Phaeospelide A is a fungal macrolide natural product; the native ecological role of the pathway remains UNCERTAIN.

BGC0002250 is centered on TtcA, a hybrid PKS-NRPS required for triticone biosynthesis in Pyrenophora tritici-repentis. Native ttcA deletion eliminates the known triticones and a broader family of related metabolites, providing direct causal evidence for pathway necessity.
ttcA encodes the hybrid PKS-NRPS core biosynthetic enzyme. The broader locus may contain tailoring functions, but the strongest direct assignment is the ttcA requirement demonstrated genetically.

Triticones were profiled from fungal culture under the defining experimental conditions. The study establishes native production and genetic dependence but does not resolve a specific environmental signal or transcriptional activation gate.
Targeted ttcA deletion, comparative metabolomics, LC-MS profiling and pathogenicity phenotyping.
Triticone A/B features were reported around m/z 278.1023 and triticone C/D-like features around m/z 280.1178; 37 additional triticone-like metabolite features were associated with TtcA.

Under the tested infection conditions, ttcA deletion did not cause an obvious reduction in pathogenicity, arguing against treating triticone production as an experimentally established essential virulence determinant.

Historical BGC0002251 links the endophytic fungus Cyanodermella asteris to astin biosynthesis. A roughly 50-kb, 13-gene cluster centered on the five-module NRPS AstN is consistent with assembly of the cyclic pentapeptide scaffold, but the MIBiG accession is now retired.

AstN is an approximately 614-kDa five-module NRPS proposed to assemble the astin peptide. AstR and AstP are implicated in precursor/building-block supply; additional cluster genes include regulatory and transport functions. No obvious halogenase was identified in the reported cluster.

Astins were produced in axenic fungal culture, supporting fungal biosynthetic autonomy. Earlier host-reinfection observations suggested possible plant-fungus interaction effects, but later work weakens any requirement for host cross-talk as a necessary production condition.
Axenic fungal cultivation, metabolite isolation, genome sequencing/mining, cluster annotation and host-reinfection studies.
AstN approximately 614 kDa; five NRPS modules; candidate cluster approximately 50 kb with 13 genes.
Astins are cyclic pentapeptide natural products known from Aster-associated material; their precise ecological function in the endophyte-host system remains UNCERTAIN.

Historical BGC0002252 represents a candidate sesquiterpene locus associated with δ6-protoilludene, illudin-type intermediates, prebovistol, bovistol B/D and strossmayerin. The proposed sequence is chemically coherent, but the canonical accession is retired and the locus assignment rests on comparative/expressional evidence rather than knockout or complete heterologous proof.

Candidate cluster functions include a 1,11-cyclizing sesquiterpene cyclase, FAD oxidoreductase, aldo-keto reductase and cytochrome P450. These annotations support the proposed oxidation/reduction sequence but are not all individually validated catalytically.
Native metabolite production and RNA-seq were used to prioritize the candidate locus. Specific environmental activation signals and direct targeted activation experiments are NR.
Natural-product isolation, structural characterization, sesquiterpene-cyclase phylogenetics, genome mining and RNA-seq-supported candidate-cluster nomination.
NR for a validated locus-specific production titer in the current retired record.
Bovistol and related illudin/protoilludene sesquiterpenes are fungal secondary metabolites; their native ecological function in C. strossmayeri remains UNCERTAIN.

BGC0002253 is associated with waikikiamides A-C and semivioxanthin-related precursors in Aspergillus sp. FM242. Genome mining identifies a coherent PKS locus, but the defining work proposed the pathway from chemical and genomic evidence rather than demonstrating complete gene-by-gene reconstruction.

SvioA: non-reducing PKS; SvioC: enoyl reductase; SvioM: O-methyltransferase; SvioL: laccase; SvioT: MFS transporter; SvioR1/SvioR2: regulatory candidates. Assignments combine annotation with pathway-context evidence.

Waikikiamides and related metabolites were isolated from cultured Aspergillus sp. FM242. Native transcriptional gating and targeted pathway-activation experiments were not resolved in the defining report.
Natural-product isolation, HRMS/NMR structure elucidation, antiproliferative assays, genome sequencing/mining and biosynthetic proposal.
Waikikiamides A and C showed antiproliferative IC50 values in the approximately 0.56-1.86 µM range in the defining study.
Waikikiamides A/C have antiproliferative activity, but the ecological function of the metabolites or locus in Aspergillus sp. FM242 remains UNCERTAIN.

BGC0002254 is an FM242 locus associated with notoamide F and related metabolites that overlap chemically with the waikikiamide study. The record supports precursor/tailoring-pathway association, but evidence is insufficient for a complete locus-to-final-product reconstruction.

Annotated functions include NotD FAD-dependent oxidase, NotE AMP-dependent synthetase/ligase, NotG/NotH cytochrome P450s and prenyltransferase-like activity among indole-associated biosynthetic genes. These functions are retained at annotation/pathway-context confidence unless directly tested.
Metabolites were observed from cultured Aspergillus sp. FM242 in the natural-product discovery context. Native regulatory triggers and targeted activation of BGC0002254 are NR.
Natural-product isolation, structure elucidation, genome mining and comparative biosynthetic annotation.
No validated locus-specific notoamide F production titer was identified in the current canonical record.
Notoamides and related prenylated indole alkaloids have diverse biological activities, but the ecological function of this specific FM242 locus is UNCERTAIN.

BGC0002255 is the lijiquinone-associated PKS locus from endophytic Ascomycota sp. F53. Genome mining linked the lijA-lijH region to the novel azaphilone lijiquinone; the cluster-level association is stronger than the available gene-by-gene biochemical resolution.

The locus contains lijA-lijH, including a PKS-centered biosynthetic architecture. Individual lij enzyme functions are not upgraded beyond the defining study/current database evidence because a detailed MIBiG biosynthesis module is absent.

Lijiquinone was discovered from an endophytic fungal isolate in a genome-mining/natural-product workflow. Specific native activation cues or targeted transcriptional activation of the lij cluster are NR.
Genome mining, fungal cultivation, metabolite isolation, LC-MS/NMR characterization and cluster association.
NR for a validated native lijiquinone titer in the current canonical record.
Lijiquinone is an azaphilone polyketide from a Taxus-associated endophyte; its native ecological function is UNCERTAIN.

BGC0002256 is an active NRPS-plus-other locus proposed for fusarochromanone, desacetylfusarochromene, fusarochromene and 4-hydroxykynurenine biosynthesis in Fusarium equiseti. Genome mining and biochemical logic support conversion of tryptophan through kynurenine-derived and prenylated intermediates, but complete heterologous reconstruction is not established.

fscA: NRPS-like oxidoreductase; fscB: transcription factor; fscC: NRPS-like tryptophan epimerase candidate; fscD: tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase; fscE: putative tryptophan 6-hydroxylase; fscG: DMATS-family prenyltransferase; fscH: kynurenine-formamidase-like hydrolase; fscI: oxidoreductase; fscJ: aromatic peroxidase; fscF remains less specifically resolved.

The pathway was investigated from a toxin-producing Fusarium context and by genome mining around characteristic tryptophan-dioxygenase/prenyltransferase functions. Specific environmental activation gates are NR.
Genome mining, pathway annotation, metabolite/precursor analysis and comparison with earlier fusarochromanone biosynthetic chemistry.
NR for a validated current locus-specific fusarochromanone titer in MIBiG.
Fusarochromanone-family metabolites are Fusarium secondary metabolites with toxic biological effects reported historically; the precise native ecological role of the fsc locus remains UNCERTAIN.

BGC0002257 is an active/SQ_A Xylaria schweinitzii PKS locus associated with rufoschweinitzin biosynthesis. The strongest direct mechanistic evidence is heterologous verification that the cluster P450 ShwC performs oxidative biaryl coupling of torachrysone-8-O-methyl ether to rufoschweinitzin, while the upstream PKS/methyltransferase steps are supported by cluster organization and pathway reconstruction rather than equivalent direct assays for every gene.

shwP: polyketide synthase; shwM1 and shwM2: O-methyltransferases; shwC: cytochrome P450 experimentally verified for oxidative coupling; shwB: metallo-beta-lactamase-family protein; shwE: EthD-superfamily protein; shwD: hypothetical protein. Only ShwC has the defining direct catalytic assignment in the primary study.

BGC access was established through heterologous expression rather than a resolved native X. schweinitzii induction regime. Rufoschweinitzin itself was originally isolated from Cortinarius rufoolivaceus; native regulatory gates in X. schweinitzii are NR.

Natural-product isolation and structure elucidation; genome mining of X. schweinitzii; heterologous expression of the encoded P450; product analysis establishing regioselective oxidative dimerization.
NR for a validated native X. schweinitzii rufoschweinitzin production titer in the canonical record.
Rufoschweinitzin is a fungal binaphthalene natural product. A specific native ecological function for BGC0002257 in X. schweinitzii is NR.

BGC0002258 is an active/SQ_A PKS locus for shimalactones A and B. ShmA alone yields preshimalactone in Aspergillus oryzae; addition of ShmB supports epoxidation followed by spontaneous oxabicyclic-ring formation and an 8π-6π electrocyclization sequence. The defining work therefore separates enzyme-catalysed precursor formation from non-enzymatic scaffold assembly.

shmA: polyketide synthase producing preshimalactone; shmB: FAD-dependent monooxygenase enabling epoxidation; shmC: transporter; shmD: iron-sulfur protein; shmE: transcription factor; shmF: oxidoreductase; shmG: membrane protein. Direct catalytic assignments are strongest for ShmA and ShmB.

Pathway chemistry was resolved by heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae and Saccharomyces cerevisiae plus in vitro/chemical analysis. Native environmental regulation in the producing Aspergillus is NR.

Candidate-cluster analysis; heterologous expression of ShmA and ShmA+ShmB; product isolation and structural characterization; in vitro epoxide studies; density-functional-theory calculations supporting spontaneous ring-forming electrocyclizations.
NR for a validated native shimalactone production titer in the canonical record.
Shimalactones A and B were reported as neuritogenic fungal polyketides. Their native ecological role is NR.

BGC0002259 is an active/SQ_A four-gene PKS-NRPS locus for beauveriolides I and III. Genome mining followed by heterologous reconstruction in Aspergillus nidulans establishes pathway sufficiency, while native detection in both ferment mycelia and fruiting bodies anchors the chemistry to C. militaris itself.

The conserved four-gene pathway includes a polyketide synthase (BesB-family) that supplies the hydroxy-fatty-acid component, an NRPS assembly enzyme, an AMP-dependent acyl-CoA ligase (BesD-family), and an additional accessory/transferase function. The core architecture is conserved across Cordycipitaceae, but substrate-specificity control is distributed and is not assigned to a single gene without direct evidence.

Beauveriolides I and III were detected in native C. militaris ferment mycelia and fruiting bodies; pathway sufficiency was tested by heterologous expression in Aspergillus nidulans. Specific native regulatory triggers are NR.

Genome mining; heterologous BGC expression in Aspergillus nidulans; LC-MS detection in native mycelia and fruiting bodies; comparative BGC analysis across Cordycipitaceae and feeding/gene-replacement follow-up studies.
NR for a validated native beauveriolide I/III production titer in the canonical record.

Beauveriolides I and III are acyl-CoA:cholesterol acyltransferase inhibitors. A later comparative study found that beauveriolide production can contribute to virulence in a host-dependent manner across related entomopathogenic fungi; a universal C. militaris ecological role is therefore UNCERTAIN.

BGC0002260 is an active/SQ_A terpene locus for trichobrasilenol, xylarenic acid B and brasilanes A/D/E/F. Heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae and in vitro enzyme assays resolve the core sequence from FPP-derived brasilane alcohol through glycosylation and P450 oxidation.

braA: terpene cyclase converting farnesyl pyrophosphate to the brasilane sesquiterpene alcohol; braB: UDP-GlcNAc-dependent N-acetylglucosamine transferase with broad donor/acceptor tolerance and some UDP-glucose activity; braC: multifunctional cytochrome P450 responsible for sequential oxygenation/epoxidation chemistry. Roles of braD and braE are less directly resolved in the defining core experiments.
Native metabolites were profiled from A. truncatum; pathway causality was tested by heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae and purified-enzyme assays. Native transcriptional gating is NR.
Metabolomics and structure elucidation; genome mining; heterologous expression; in vitro BraB glycosyltransferase assays with alternative donors/acceptors; P450 functional reconstruction.
BraA sequence showed 70.9% similarity to the previously characterized Tvi09626 brasilane cyclase; a validated native product titer is NR.
The products are oxygenated brasilane sesquiterpenoids and glycosides; a specific native ecological function in A. truncatum is NR.

BGC0002261 is an active/SQ_A luc1-luc8 cluster centered on the hybrid PKS-NRPS Luc5. Δluc5 abolishes lucilactaene and NG-391; Δluc1 accumulates demethylated analogues. Follow-up Δluc2 and Δluc3 strains establish Luc2 involvement in C-20 hydroxylation and support Luc3 aldehyde-dehydrogenase participation, correcting earlier mechanistic ambiguity.

luc5: hybrid PKS-NRPS required for backbone formation; luc1: methyltransferase required for carboxyl methylation; luc2: cytochrome P450 implicated by knockout in C-20 hydroxylation; luc3: aldehyde dehydrogenase supported by knockout/intermediate accumulation; luc4: MFS transporter; luc6: esterase; luc7: eEF1B-gamma-like protein; luc8: protease-like protein. Functions of luc4/6/7/8 are primarily annotation-level.
Native Fusarium sp. RK97-94 cultures in FDY medium were used for knockout metabolite profiling; specific environmental activation gates beyond producing culture conditions are NR.
Degenerate-PCR/genome walking; Δluc5 and Δluc1 knockouts with UPLC-MS; structural analysis of accumulated analogues; later Δluc2 and Δluc3 knockouts; antimalarial and cell-growth assays.
Lucilactaene antimalarial IC50 was reported as 0.063 µg/mL (approximately 160 nM) in the defining study; artemisinin control was 0.0085 µg/mL (approximately 30 nM). Native production titer is NR.
Lucilactaene is a p53-independent G1 cell-cycle inhibitor and shows potent in-vitro antimalarial activity; demethylated analogues lose these activities. Native ecological function in Fusarium is NR.

BGC0002262 is canonically labeled PKS, but the defining study experimentally resolves a dedicated FAS/citrate-synthase alkyl-citrate pathway: SpofasA/B supply a decanoyl unit, SpoE couples it to oxaloacetate, SpoL/SpoK generate octyl itaconic acid, SpoG oxygenates, and SpoH/SpoJ together are required for final sporothriolide formation. Sporochartines arise non-enzymatically from sporothriolide plus trienylfuranol A.

spofasA/spofasB: fungal FAS α/β subunits; spoE: citrate synthase; spoL: methylcitrate dehydratase; spoK: decarboxylase; spoG: dioxygenase; spoH/spoJ: two lactonases that act jointly in final product formation; spoC/spoF: transporters; spoD: transcriptional regulator; spoI: cupin-domain protein with unresolved biosynthetic role.

Native H. monticulosa transformation/knockout work was combined with Aspergillus oryzae heterologous expression and in-vitro assays. Producing versus non-producing expression states were examined, but a singular environmental activation trigger is NR.

Genome sequencing and comparative cluster identification; simultaneous knockout of FAS/citrate-synthase functions; heterologous spo-gene combinations in A. oryzae; in-vitro SpoG and hydrolase assays; structural characterization; non-enzymatic Diels-Alder tests.
NR for a validated native sporothriolide titer in the canonical record; pathway experiments instead resolved intermediate identities and gene-dependence qualitatively.

Sporothriolide was studied as an antifungal metabolite; in-vitro work also identified a hydrolase activity likely contributing to producer self-resistance. The broader native ecological role remains UNCERTAIN.

BGC0002263 is currently retired. Historically it represents a proposed 68.2-kb, 21-ORF spiromarmycin locus in Spiromastix sp. SCSIO F190, centered on reducing iterative PKS Spm13 and nonreducing iterative PKS Spm12. ^13C-acetate incorporation and symbiont-dependent transcription/product changes strongly support a fungal polyketide origin but do not provide gene-by-gene knockout causality.

spm13: reducing iterative PKS with KS-AT-DH-ER-KR-ACP domains; spm12: nonreducing iterative PKS with KS-AT-ACP-TE domains; spm14: proposed hydroxylase in the postulated pathway; remaining spm ORFs are largely annotation/model-based in the defining report.

The endobacterium Alcaligenes faecalis SCSIO B001 resides within fungal mycelium and strongly upregulates spiromarmycin production. Antibiotic suppression of B001 decreases production, and the authors could not obtain a stable endobacterium-free fungus.

Fungal/endobacterial co-culture characterization; antibiotic perturbation; genome sequencing and PKS-cluster mining; spm12/spm13 expression analysis; [1-13C]- and [2-13C]-acetate feeding; NMR/structure elucidation and antimicrobial assays.

In 20-day isotope-feeding cultures, labeled spiromarmycin epimer fractions were isolated at 8.5 and 12.5 mg for [1-13C]acetate and 12.6 and 13.3 mg for [2-13C]acetate experiments; these are experimental isolation yields, not native production titers.

Spiromarmycin showed antibacterial/antifungal activity but did not inhibit the resident endobacterium B001, supporting a proposed protective role for the fungal-bacterial symbiotic pair; ecological protection remains an inference rather than a direct fitness demonstration.

BGC0002264 is an active/SQ_A 12-gene NRPS locus for hancockiamides A-F. Heterologous expression in Aspergillus nidulans confirms cluster sufficiency; biochemical and feeding studies resolve trans-cinnamate activation/transfer by Hkm11 and methylenedioxy-bridge formation by Hkm5, while several earlier piperazine-tailoring steps remain mechanistically proposed.

hkm10 and hkm11: single-module NRPSs; Hkm11 directly activates/transfers trans-cinnamate; hkm9: NmrA-like reductase proposed with Hkm10 in piperazine formation; hkm5: P450 directly forming methylenedioxy bridges; hkm12: phenylalanine ammonia-lyase, dispensable but boosts cinnamoylated products; hkm3: acetyltransferase; hkm4/6/7/8 encode proposed oxygenation/methylation functions.

Native hancockiamides were isolated from A. hancockii; biosynthetic access was established by heterologous expression in A. nidulans, truncated-cluster constructs, in-vitro assays and substrate feeding. Native environmental regulation is NR.

Genome analysis; heterologous expression of full and truncated hkm clusters; in-vitro Hkm11 assays; substrate feeding; P450 functional analysis; isolation/structure elucidation of additional congeners.
NR for a validated native hancockiamide production titer in the canonical record.
Hancockiamides are unusual N-cinnamoylated piperazine natural products. A defined native ecological role or validated therapeutic activity is NR in the defining pathway study.

BGC0002265 is currently retired because of missing gene annotations. The defining heterologous work nevertheless establishes a three-enzyme atranorin route: Atr1/PKS23 alone forms 4-O-demethylbarbatic acid, Atr2 performs stepwise C-9 oxidation to the aldehyde proatranorin III, and Atr3 methylates the carboxyl group; coexpression of atr1-atr3 yields atranorin.

atr1 (PKS23): nonreducing polyketide synthase that forms/depsidically couples 3-methylorsellinic-acid units to 4-O-demethylbarbatic acid; atr2: cytochrome P450 responsible for C-9 hydroxylation/further oxidation to aldehyde; atr3: O-methyltransferase/carboxyl methylase; atr4: transporter-associated candidate not required for the minimal three-gene heterologous reconstruction.

A clean heterologous fungal host was used for single-gene and combinatorial expression, and authentic S. alpinum voucher chemistry provided comparison. Native lichen symbiotic regulation of the pathway remains NR.
Genetic dereplication; clean-host heterologous expression of atr1, atr1+atr2, atr1+atr3 and atr1+atr2+atr3; HPLC, LC-MS/MS and NMR; comparison with authentic S. alpinum voucher material.
NR for a validated native atranorin production titer in the canonical record.
Atranorin is a major cortical lichen depside in S. alpinum. The pathway study establishes its natural occurrence and biosynthesis but does not directly quantify a native ecological fitness function.

BGC0002266 is an active/SQ_A PKS-terpene locus for calidoustenes A-C within a larger experimentally reconstructed drimane-ester family. DrtB makes drimenol, DrtD performs multiple P450 oxidations, DrtC generates carboxylic-acid/γ-butyrolactone functionality, DrtA supplies C6/C8 polyketide side chains, DrtF tunes their oxidation state, and DrtE transfers acyl chains to the drimane scaffold.

drtA: polyketide synthase producing variable C6/C8 acyl chains; drtB: fungal drimenol cyclase; drtC: FAD-binding oxidoreductase involved in carboxyl/γ-butyrolactone formation; drtD: cytochrome P450 catalyzing multiple drimenol hydroxylations/oxidations; drtE: acyltransferase accepting ACP-activated and diverse CoA-ester substrates; drtF: short-chain dehydrogenase controlling side-chain oxidation/saturation.

The FUP1-FUP5 cluster is strongly validated by native genetics and LC-MS/MS. FUP1 disruption eliminates fusaproliferin; FUP4 controls oxidation toward terpestacin; FUP5 acetylates terpestacin to fusaproliferin, with FUP5 loss abolishing FUP and increasing terpestacin. FUP3 is also required for downstream products. FUP2 remains the principal gene-level uncertainty because a knockout was not obtained.

MpMS (MPH_02178/EKG20455) is a bifunctional class-I triterpene synthase. Heterologous yeast expression produced macrophomene and purified recombinant MpMS efficiently converted DMAPP/IPP to the same product through HexPP. The canonical source's source-category SQ_A label is retained as provenance but does not erase the stronger direct experimental evidence.

The P. ipomoeae IasaF13 indole-diterpene locus is a strong comparative-genomic assignment to a broad native chemical profile spanning paspaline, paxilline and multiple terpendoles. The canonical physical interval JN587270.1:5500-25800 is well defined. Core idtG/idtM/idtB/idtC and peripheral idtP/idtQ/idtK/idtF assignments are supported by conserved pathway architecture, but direct P. ipomoeae knockout/reconstruction evidence is lacking and idtS remains functionally unresolved.
